1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version
16	Prelude depends on) rather than from memory. Run `koda-review` before calling a
17	change finished.
18	
19	Koda is the npm package `@kodalang/core`, pinned in `package.json`, and it ships
20	its skills. The ones in `.claude/skills/` are copies of the installed package's;
21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run
22	`npm run skills` to copy them again, and read what changed.
23	
24	## Working here
25	
26	- `npm start` runs Prelude on http://localhost:4200 (`PORT` to change it).
27	  Views are cached when the server starts: restart it after changing one.
28	- `npm test` runs the tests (node --test). Add tests for what you build.
29	- The desktop app: `npm run build:shell` builds `tauri/src-tauri` (about 10
30	  minutes from cold) into `dist-shell/Prelude.exe`. `npm run test:shell` runs its
31	  Rust tests. The app is a window on the server: it uses one already answering
32	  `/health` on localhost:4200 (`npm start`), or else starts `node start.js`
33	  itself (Prelude's folder is found above the exe, or `--root`/`PRELUDE_ROOT`;
34	  its output goes to `~/.prelude/server.log`) and stops it on quit. `--server
35	  <url>` or `PRELUDE_URL` p

1	// A project's architecture (prelude/architecture): a design of "kind":
2	// "architecture", one per project (R-p0j), kept as markdown files that agents
3	// read before they change anything (R-c2m) and that Prelude reads to show
4	// them on the project's Architecture pages (D-e8y). Nothing is written twice:
5	// the files are the one source, and what's derived (each part's "used by",
6	// decisions and findings, the map's layers) is prepared here.
7	//
8	// The files, in the design's architecture/ folder (the format the drafting
9	// agent is told: architecturePrompt in agent.js):
10	//
11	//   overview.md          # title, a summary, "## Layers" (a numbered list, top
12	//                        to bottom) and "## Principles" ("- **Title.** Why.")
13	//   parts/<id>.md        # title, then a header of "key: value" lines (layer,
14	//                        kind: module | process | outside, short, files: globs,
15	//                        uses: part ids), a summary, and "## Responsible for",
16	//                        "## Not its job", "## Owns" lists
17	//   decisions/<id>.md    # title, a header (status, date, parts, supersedes),
18	//                        then "## Context", "## Decision", "## Consequences"
19	//   flows/<id>.md        # title, a summary, numbered steps "part-id: text",
20	//                        and an optional "decisions:" header
21	//
22	// The check (R-4vx, R-k5e; D-r0k): after every turn that changes code, the
23	// code is read again - each file's imports (JavaScript and TypeScript, so
24	// far), each file mapped to its part by `files` - and these are reported: a
25	// use a part doesn't say it may make, a use of a part in a layer above, a
26	// code file no part names, and a named file that isn't there. A file is
27	// expected to belong to a part when it's under a folder a part's glob names
28	// (server/views/** covers server/views/, recursively), or beside a file a
29	// part names (server/main.js covers server/'s own files).

1	# Prelude — plan
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent. Built with Koda.
4	It starts as the smallest thing that works: **pick a folder, chat with an agent,
5	watch the design appear.** Features are added only after we've decided where they fit
6	in that model.
7	
8	## The model
9	
10	There are five nouns, and nothing else until a new one earns its place (the fifth, Fix, earned its place in step 11).
11	
12	| Noun | What it is | Where it lives |
13	| --- | --- | --- |
14	| **Project** | What you're designing (and later building), kept in a folder you chose, usually a repo | anywhere on disk |
15	| **Design** | A named body of work (screens + notes) built up over many sessions; usually one feature | `prelude/<design>/` |
16	| **Session** | One conversation with the agent, contributing to one design or one fix | `prelude/<design>/sessions/<id>/` |
17	| **Screen** | One page of the design | `prelude/<design>/screens/NN-name.html` |
18	| **Fix** | One problem in a project, outside any one design, worked on in sessions on a branch of its own | `prelude/fixes/<slug>/` |
19	
20	The interface has two surfaces, modeled on OrchestratR's design session:
21	
22	- **Chat**: the current session's transcript, with filters, the message box, and a
23	  session switcher ("New session" starts another). Any session can be continued on
24	  the machine that started it.
25	- **Design**: the preview, with a screen picker, Refresh, Open in browser and Pop out.
26	
27	Pop out moves the Design surface to its own window, so one window holds the chat and
28	the other holds the design.
29	
30	**Project, folder, app.** People see *project* for the whole of it: its designs, its
31	design system and shell, and in time its app. *Folder* means only where it is on disk
32	("the project's folder", a reference folder). *App* means only the built, running app
33	and its stack. The code keeps its older names (`folders.js`, `app.folders`,

1	// The sandboxed half of the Eta host: renders a design's views, and nothing else.
2	//
3	// Eta templates compile to JavaScript, and a design's views are written by the
4	// agent. Rendered inside Prelude's server they could do anything Prelude can,
5	// undoing the fences on what the agent may read and write. So they render
6	// here, in a process of their own started under Node's permission model
7	// (renderers.js): it may read the folder and Prelude's own files, and may not
8	// write, start processes or load native code. (Node's permission model
9	// doesn't yet cover the network; that remains a known gap.)
10	//
11	// Messages, over the IPC channel:
12	//   in:  { id, page: { views, template, data }, layout?: { views, template, data },
13	//          regions?: { <name>: { views, template, data, location } }, query? }
14	//   out: { id, html } or { id, error }
15	// The layout, when there is one, gets the rendered page as `it.body`, and each
16	// rendered region (an overlay presented over the page) as
17	// `it.regions.<name> = { html, location }`, to print inside the region it offers.
18	// The page (and every region) sees the request's query string as `it.$query`,
19	// so a search or filter form can show what was asked.

3	A fourth kind of design, besides features, the design system and the shell:
4	**the project's architecture**, kept as markdown files that agents read and
5	shown to the team on the project's Architecture pages, the way the design
6	system's gallery shows the system. Prelude's own architecture (from
7	`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plan.md`) is the sample data.
8	
9	This design is those pages: views at Prelude's own URLs
10	(`/f/:folder/architecture/…`), with states shaped as Prelude's model of the
11	files would be.
12	
13	## Decided (2026-10-22, with the person)
14	
15	- **A design of `"kind": "architecture"`, one per project** (R-p0j), like the
16	  system and the shell. Its sessions shape it ("draft it from the code").
17	- **Prelude reads the files itself**, as it reads RULES.md, so nothing is
18	  written twice (D-e8y in the sample). The real architecture design will
19	  have no states; this design's states stand in for what Prelude reads.
20	- **Markdown, a file per thing**, in the design's `architecture/` folder (as
21	  the system's is `system/`):
22	  - `overview.md`: a summary, the layers in order, the principles (title, why);
23	  - `parts/<id>.md`: a header (title, layer, kind: module / process / outside,
24	    `files` globs, `uses` part ids), then sections: Responsible for, Not its
25	    job, Owns;
26	  - `decisions/<id>.md`: a header (title, status, date, parts, supersedes),
27	    then Context, Decision, Consequences. Ids are `D-` + three random
28	    characters, so branches never clash;
29	  - `flows/<id>.md`: a title, a summary, numbered steps each starting with
30	    the part's id.
31	  Prelude prepares what's derived: each part's "used by", decisions and
32	  findings, and the map's layers.
33	- **Proposed decisions are accepted by merging** (R-7tq): an agent's
34	  proposal is reviewed with its branch, and Prelude marks it accepted at
35	  merge (as it clears a route's `from`).

I've drafted the architecture from the code, and the Architecture page beside the chat now shows it. I haven't run the check against these files yet; Prelude runs it when this turn ends.

**What's there**
- **`overview.md`**: a one-paragraph summary, seven layers (Windows, Entry points, Pages, Agent and live state, Designs and hosting, Project files, Outside) and seven principles taken from the plan's ground rules.
- **21 parts.** They're grouped by what they're responsible for, not one per file. Every JavaScript file in `server/`, `tools/` and `start.js` belongs to one, and each part's `uses` matches its actual imports. Examples: `server`, `pages`, `turns`, `agent`, `host` plus the sandboxed `renderer` process, `branches`, `designs`, `sessions`. There are four outside parts: Claude CLI, git/gh/az, Koda and Eta, and local programs.
- **7 decisions**: the project's folder is the database, the sandboxed renderer, a separate origin for designs, live state kept on the server, a branch and worktree per design, the CLI with ordinary file tools, and the desktop app as a window on the server.
- **2 flows**: a message to the agent, and a design's page in the preview.

**Choices you may want to change**
- `home.js` and `turns.js` import each other's modules. That's why the page models, turns and views all share the Pages layer.
- `test/` isn't in any part. The check only looks at folders a part names, so tests aren't reported.

**Questions for you** (also listed in NOTES.md)
1. The plan doesn't date two of the decisions, so I estimated: the sandboxed renderer (D-r7s) as 2026-10-15 and branches (D-b9k) as 2026-10-17. Do you know the real dates?
2. `architecture.js` imports `home.js` only for its `ago` time helper. Should that helper move lower down?
3. Should `runs.js`, which starts the built app, be its own part instead of sitting in the design host?

I've made both changes:

1. **Dates:** both undated decisions are now dated 2026-10-15. Those are the sandboxed renderer (D-r7s) and branches (D-b9k).
2. **`runs.js`:** it's now its own part, **App runs** (`runs`), in the Designs and hosting layer. It uses `host` (for the `call` helper in `hosts.js`) and `designs`. I removed it from the design host's files and responsibilities, moved `runs.json` across with it, and added `runs` to the server's uses.

On question 2, "lower down" meant a lower layer. The parts are stacked in layers, and a part should only use parts in its own layer or below. `architecture.js` (the code that checks the code against these files) imports `home.js` (the Home page's model) for just one thing: `ago`, which turns a time into words like "2 minutes ago". So the checker depends on a page model.

That's allowed today, because both are in the Pages layer. But a page model is about the last thing I'd expect the checker to depend on. My suggestion is to move `ago` and similar small word helpers into their own module in a low layer. Then the checker, and anything else that needs them, wouldn't import a page.

It's a small code change, and this session can only write the architecture, so a fix or build session would have to make it. I've left it as an open question in NOTES.md. It's fine to keep it as is if you'd rather not bother.
